artifacts.title: Magnetic susceptibility artifact
artifacts.explanation: Magnetic susceptibility artifacts happen when materials with different magnetic properties disturb the main magnetic field, causing local B0 inhomogeneity.
artifacts.visual_description: Signal voids, local distortion, or signal pile-up can appear near metal, air-tissue interfaces, or other strong susceptibility boundaries.

remedies.text: Remove metallic objects when possible and screen the imaging setup carefully.
Use careful shimming and consider sequences or parameters that reduce susceptibility sensitivity.

artifacts.title: B0 inhomogeneity effect
artifacts.explanation: B0 inhomogeneity causes spins to dephase faster and can shift signal spatially, especially in sequences sensitive to field variation.
artifacts.visual_description: Images may show geometric warping, local stretching or compression, and signal dropout in affected regions.

remedies.text: Reduce echo time when possible and use acquisition choices that are less sensitive to B0 variation.

artifacts.title: B1 inhomogeneity effect
artifacts.explanation: B1 inhomogeneity occurs when RF excitation is spatially uneven, so spins are not flipped as intended across the field of view.
artifacts.visual_description: The image can show shading or broad regional intensity variation, with some areas appearing darker or brighter than expected.

remedies.text: Use RF shimming, dielectric pads, or a dual-transmit setup when available.

artifacts.title: RF interferences
artifacts.explanation: RF interference is caused by unwanted radiofrequency sources leaking into the MRI signal chain or acquisition environment.
artifacts.visual_description: A narrow bright or dark line can cross the image, often resembling a zipper-like stripe in a consistent direction.

remedies.text: Check room shielding, door closure, cables, coils, and nearby RF-emitting equipment.
Repeat the scan after removing or isolating the suspected interference source.
